text: Agile methodology is a popular way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of doing everything at once, teams work in short phases called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Each sprint focuses on completing a set of tasks chosen from a backlog, which is a prioritized list of all the work that needs to be done. To make tasks clear, teams break them down into user stories, which are short descriptions of a feature from a customer’s perspective. Every day, team members have a quick meeting called a standup, where they share what they did yesterday and what they plan to do today. This approach supports iterative development, meaning teams deliver small pieces of a product early and often, then improve them based on feedback. Because of this, changes are easier to make, and the final product is more likely to meet real user needs.
